summary: Today’s pulse tracks John Fetterman vehemently backs Schumer for Senate majority leader and says he’s ‘considering things’ on 2028 re-election – live, Man hired by Russia spied on Silicon Valley tech and defense company, feds say, and Senate Republicans rejects war powers bill to halt fighting in Iran. Across Guardian, Ars Technica, and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are republicans, senate, and election. In the background, Traumatized teens sue school, cops after Doritos bag triggers AI gun alert and Grand Theft Auto fans skip work and pull all-nighters to play new instalment keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: John Fetterman vehemently backs Schumer for Senate majority leader and says he’s ‘considering things’ on 2028 re-election – live
headlines.description: US senator from Pennsylvania also took shot at Chris Van Hollen, who is challenging Schumer for Democratic leadership The Times reports that employees at the NSA’s Maryland headquarters are under “code orange” for Thursday day shift, which requires non-essential workers are to stay home unless contacted by their supervisors. A secret, closed-door election: Unlike the public speaker of the House vote, where lawmakers cast ballots on the chamber floor, the Senate leadership contest takes place behind closed doors. Senators vote by secret ballot, and individual votes are not disclosed. The winner only needs a caucus majority: The Democratic leadership race is decided solely by members of the party’s Senate caucus. Now that Democrats are set to have 56 seats in the new year, the winner will need secure 29 votes for the top role. The vote is scheduled for next month: As things stand, the election is set for 1 December . Both incumbent senators and incoming Democratic members will participate, while retiring and outgoing senators will not vote, despite many having publicly weighed in on the race. Republicans choose their leaders separately: Republicans hold their own closed-door leadership elections in both chambers. Earlier this month, House Republicans selected hardliner Jim Jordan as their leader after Mike Johnson opted not to run for minority leader. In the Senate, Republicans unanimously backed John Thune to continue leading the conference.

headlines.title: Senate Republicans rejects war powers bill to halt fighting in Iran
headlines.description: Measure fails 48-51 with GOP members again defending war that played a role in costing them midterm elections The Senate on Thursday rejected a war powers resolution aimed at forcing Donald Trump to halt fighting with Iran, with Republicans once again defending a conflict that played a major role in their sweeping midterm election losses. The House of Representatives had approved the resolution in September, and it was the first to be voted on by either chamber since the 3 November vote in which the GOP lost control of both chambers of Congress beginning next year.

headlines.description: Lawsuit: Over 99% of school system’s AI gun alerts were false positives.

headlines.title: Grand Theft Auto fans skip work and pull all-nighters to play new instalment
headlines.description: Hotly anticipated Bonnie and Clyde-inspired adventure GTA VI has gamers glued to their screens around the world Grand Theft Auto fans around the world pulled all-nighters, skipped work and school, and attended overnight launch parties to vicariously embark on police chases and coordinate robberies as the latest instalment of the eagerly anticipated series arrived. GTA VI, a Bonnie and Clyde-inspired crime adventure game set in the fictional US state of Leonida, was launched at midnight on Wednesday after a 13-year wait.

headlinePool.title: John Cornyn blocks Trump judicial nominee after Senate shouting match with Ted Cruz
headlinePool.description: Outgoing senator withheld ‘blue slip’ from T Elliot Gaiser, blocking his appointment to northern Texas district court An outgoing Republican senator blocked one of Donald Trump ’s judicial nominations on Wednesday, throwing a wrench in the party’s plans to approve the US president’s picks before Democrats take control of Congress. John Cornyn of Texas, who is leaving the US Senate after nearly 24 years following his primary loss to a Trump-backed challenger, told the Associated Press he would not support T Elliot Gaiser, a 37-year-old official in the justice department, to serve on a district court in northern Texas.

headlinePool.title: Judge bans Trump’s restrictions on HIV funds for transgender patients
headlinePool.description: Federal court rules providers can acknowledge gender identity and provide gender-affirming care The Trump administration cannot impose restrictions barring healthcare providers that receive certain federal HIV-treatment ⁠funds from acknowledging the gender identity ⁠of their transgender patients ​or from providing them with gender-affirming care, a federal judge ruled on Thursday. US district judge William Young in Boston sided with a group of national HIV medical associations and ⁠healthcare providers that challenged grant funding conditions imposed by the administration last year after Trump signed an executive order prohibiting federal funding for what he calls “gender ideology”.

Judges have put Trump's arch and golf course on hold, but only for a matter of days
headlinePool.description: A federal judge has twice delayed construction of Trump's arch. Another is keeping East Potomac Park open. The proposed golf course redesign got mixed feedback from a federal arts panel on Thursday.

headlinePool.title: Howard-era minister Sharman Stone dies via voluntary assisted dying, aged 75
headlinePool.description: The former Liberal MP had fought a long battle against glioblastoma, an aggressive form of brain cancer Stone died aged 75 on Wednesday surrounded by family after a long fight against glioblastoma, an aggressive form of brain cancer. She was minister for workforce participation from 2006-07.

headlinePool.title: ‘Welsh can tell any story’: Cymraeg dub of Star Wars premieres in Cardiff
headlinePool.description: Actors Mark Lewis Jones and Osian Morgan, who voiced characters in dub of 1977 film, among guests on red carpet It has been a memorable few days for Wales. At the weekend, the men’s rugby team secured a historic win against New Zealand – their first victory over the All Blacks in more than 70 years. Then on Thursday evening came another culturally significant moment when Cardiff rolled out the red carpet to celebrate the first Welsh-language dub of the Star Wars franchise. Stars of stage and screen who voiced the words of Luke Skywalker, Darth Vader, C-3PO et al in Welsh (Cymraeg) over the original 1977 Star Wars film took the plaudits at the Cineworld Cardiff screening.

headlinePool.title: Prison authorities consider whether Russell Brand harassed victims with YouTube message
headlinePool.description: Ministry of Justice weighs up comments issued through rapist’s wife as PM asks: ‘Why are we having to hear from him?’ The prison authorities are weighing up whether Russell Brand harassed his victims by issuing comments through his wife insisting he was not guilty of rape and sexual assault. After Andy Burnham called on Google to take down the statement from YouTube, a continuing Ministry of Justice inquiry is focusing on whether Brand has broken rules that are supposed to prevent “serious distress” to the victims of crime.

headlinePool.title: Man arrested after ‘horrific’ knife attack on Bradford councillor
headlinePool.description: Politicians call attack on independent councillor Ibrar Ali canvassing in Bradford Moor ward ‘deeply disturbing’ Politicians have described an attack on a councillor who was canvassing in Bradford as “horrific” and “deeply disturbing”, after a man was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder. A 32-year-old man is in custody suspected of attacking Ibrar Ali at about 11am on Thursday as the independent councillor was door-knocking in his Bradford Moor ward, leaving him with a stab wound in the leg.

headlinePool.description: European allies of Ukraine say they have a "united" negotiating position at a summit in Berlin.
